extracted.intended_audience: Applicants submitting ANDAs or NDAs (and their regulatory/legal teams)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedural standards for preparing, amending, notifying, and submitting Abbreviated New Drug Applications (ANDAs) and related paragraph IV patent certifications, and for FDA's review communications and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment after finding of infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who submitted a paragraph IV certification and is sued for patent infringement must submit an amendment to change its certification if a court enters a final decision (no appeal possible) or signs and enters a settlement order or consent decree that includes a finding that the patent is infringed, unless that final decision/settlement also finds the patent invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the amendment, the applicant must certify that the patent will expire on a specific date or, for a patent claiming a method of use, may instead provide a statement under paragraph (a)(12)(iii) if the applicant amends the ANDA so it is no longer seeking approval for the method of use claimed by the patent. Once such an amendment is submitted, the ANDA will no longer be considered to contain a paragraph IV certification. If a final judgment finds the patent to be invalid and infringed, an amended certification is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment after request to remove patent from list
rubrics_metrics.description: If an NDA holder requests removal of a patent or patent information from the list and no ANDA applicant is eligible for 180-day exclusivity based on a paragraph IV to that patent, the patent/information will be removed and any applicant with a pending ANDA who made a certification must submit an amendment to withdraw its certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amendment must state the reason for withdrawing the certification (that the patent has been removed). If first applicant exclusivity exists, the patent remains listed until exclusivity has expired or been extinguished; after that, removal triggers the withdrawal amendment requirement. Once the amendment to withdraw is submitted, the ANDA will no longer be considered to contain a paragraph IV certification. If removal leaves no patents listed for the listed drug, the applicant must submit an amended certification reflecting that there are no relevant patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend certification when it becomes inaccurate / when new patent issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided, an applicant must amend a submitted certification or statement if, at any time before approval of the ANDA, the applicant learns the submitted certification/statement is no longer accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If after ANDA submission a new patent is issued that, to the applicant's best knowledge, claims the reference listed drug or an approved use for it and must be filed under §§505(b)/(c) and §314.53, the applicant must submit the appropriate patent certification/statement. For paragraph IV certifications, the certification must not be submitted earlier than the first working day after the patent is published in the list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial certification or disclosure statement required
rubrics_metrics.description: An ANDA must contain a financial certification or disclosure statement as required by part 54 of this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: DESI / DESI-like product compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ANDA is for a duplicate of a drug subject to FDA's DESI review (or DESI-like review) and the drug evaluated is a listed drug, the applicant must comply with the provisions applicable to ANDAs (paragraph (a) of this section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Archival copy requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must submit a complete archival copy of the ANDA; FDA will maintain the archival copy during the review to permit reviewers access and to maintain a complete copy in one place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portions of the archival copy may be submitted in any form agreed to by applicant and FDA, except as otherwise stated (e.g., labeling must be electronic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling electronic submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of required labeling (package insert or professional labeling), including all text, tables, and figures, must be submitted to the agency in electronic format as described, in addition to formatted label copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions under this paragraph must comply with part 11 except for specified exclusions (§11.10(a),(c)-(h),(k) and corresponding §11.30 requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic format submissions must be processable
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic format submissions must be in a form that FDA can process, review, and archive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA will periodically issue guidance on method of transmission, media, file formats, and organization of files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review copy structure (two sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: For ANDAs, the applicant must submit a review copy containing two separate sections: one containing specified information (paragraphs (a)(2)-(6),(8),(9) and §505(j)(2)(A)(vii) plus analytical procedures for labs) and the other containing information from paragraphs (a)(3),(7),(8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each section must contain a copy of the application form described under paragraph (a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Field copy requirement and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must submit a field copy that contains the technical section described and a copy of the application form, and must certify that the field copy is a true copy of the technical section contained in the archival and review copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant (other than a foreign applicant) must include a statement certifying that a field copy of each amendment has been sent to the applicant's home FDA district office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice recipients for paragraph IV certification
rubrics_metrics.description: For each patent to which a paragraph IV certification is submitted, the applicant must send notice by registered/certified mail or by a designated delivery service to: (1) each owner of the patent or its designated representative, and (2) the holder of the approved NDA for the listed drug claimed by the patent (or the NDA holder's attorney/agent/authorized official).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name/address of patent owner or NDA holder may be obtained from PTO or the FDA Central Document Room/Orange Book staff. This paragraph does not apply to a method-of-use patent that does not claim a use for which the applicant is seeking approval. An alternative method of sending notice is allowed only if FDA agrees in advance that it will produce acceptable documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for sending paragraph IV notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must send the notice on or after the date it receives a paragraph IV acknowledgment letter from FDA, but not later than 20 days after the postmark date on the acknowledgment letter; the 20-day clock begins the day after the postmark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 20th day falls on weekend or Federal holiday, the 20th day is the next non-weekend/non-holiday. Any notice sent before the applicant's receipt of the paragraph IV acknowledgment letter, or before the first working day after the patent is published in the list, is invalid. Applicant must submit an amendment certifying that the notice was provided and met content requirements; a copy of the notice itself need not be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of paragraph IV notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must cite §505(j)(2)(B)(iv) and include (at minimum): statement that FDA received applicant's ANDA with required data; the ANDA number; statement applicant received the paragraph IV acknowledgment letter; established name of proposed drug; active ingredient, strength, dosage form; patent number and expiration date; a detailed statement of the factual and legal basis for the opinion that the patent is invalid, unenforceable, or will not be infringed; (additional items described).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed statement must include for each claim alleged not infringed a full explanation why not infringed; for each claim alleged invalid or unenforceable a full explanation of grounds. If alleging noninfringement and preserving option to later file declaratory judgment, notice must be accompanied by an offer of confidential access to the ANDA for sole/limited purpose of evaluating infringement. If applicant has no US place of business, include name/address of US agent authorized to accept service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice for amendments or supplements containing paragraph IV
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after receipt of a paragraph IV acknowledgment letter, an applicant submits an amendment or supplement that includes a paragraph IV certification, the applicant must send the required notice at the same time the amendment or supplement is submitted to FDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amendment is submitted before receipt of paragraph IV acknowledgment, the applicant must send notice per the timing rules; timely provision of notice may affect FDA's determination of who is a 'first applicant' for exclusivity purposes (based on date of submission of amendment containing paragraph IV). Amendments to seek approval of different strength also require notice as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of timely sending and receipt of notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must amend its ANDA to provide documentation of the date of receipt of the paragraph IV notice by each person provided the notice; this amendment must be submitted to FDA within 30 days after the last date on which notice was received by a person provided the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amendment must include documentation that the notice was sent in compliance with timing requirements and a dated printout of the Orange Book entry that includes the subject patent. FDA will accept registered mail receipt, certified mail receipt, or designated delivery service receipt as adequate documentation of date sent; and return receipt, signature proof of delivery, or a letter acknowledging receipt as adequate documentation of date received. Other documentation forms only if FDA agreed in advance. A copy of the notice itself need not be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start of 45-day period after notice receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: If the section's requirements are met, FDA will presume the notice to be complete and sufficient and will count the day following the date of receipt of the notice by the patent owner and by the approved NDA holder (or their representatives) as the first day of the 45-day period provided in section 505(j)(5)(B)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA may, if the applicant provides a written statement that a later date should be used, count from that later date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated delivery service definition
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of notice delivery, a 'designated delivery service' means a delivery service that: (i) is available to the general public throughout the United States; (ii) records electronically to its database or marks on the cover the date the item was given to the trade/business for delivery; and (iii) provides overnight or 2-day delivery service throughout the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA may periodically issue guidance regarding designated delivery services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bioequivalence study reporting in amendments to unapproved ANDA
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may amend an unapproved ANDA to revise or provide additional information. Amendments containing bioequivalence studies must contain reports of all bioequivalence studies conducted by the applicant on the same drug product formulation, unless previously submitted to FDA in the ANDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete study report must be submitted for any BE study upon which the applicant relies for approval. For other BE studies on the same formulation, the applicant may submit a complete or summary report. If a summary report is submitted and FDA determines there may be BE issues, FDA may require submission of a complete report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of significant-data amendment on initial review cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an amendment containing significant data or information before the end of the initial review cycle constitutes an agreement between FDA and the applicant to extend the initial review cycle only for the time necessary to review that significant data and for no more than 180 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on amending ANDA to refer to different listed drug
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may not amend an ANDA to seek approval of a drug referring to a listed drug that is different from the reference listed drug identified in the ANDA; such a change of reference listed drug must be submitted as a new ANDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph applies if, before approval, a different listed drug is approved that is a pharmaceutical equivalent to the product in the ANDA and designated as a reference listed drug. Notwithstanding the limitation, an applicant may amend the ANDA to seek approval of a different strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent certification requirements for certain amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment to an ANDA is required to contain an appropriate patent certification (or a recertification for a previously submitted paragraph IV) if approval is sought for: (i) adding a new indication/condition of use; (ii) adding a new strength; (iii) making other than minor changes in product formulation; or (iv) changing the physical form or crystalline structure of the active ingredient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amendment does not contain a patent certification or statement, the applicant must verify the proposed change is not one of the listed types of amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplements and changes to approved ANDA must follow §§314.70 & 314.71
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must comply with §§314.70 and 314.71 regarding submission of supplemental ANDAs and other changes to an approved ANDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may not supplement an ANDA to seek approval referencing a different listed drug than the current reference listed drug; a change of reference listed drug must be a new ANDA, though seeking approval for a different strength is permitted as a supplement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postmarketing reporting and recordkeeping obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant with an approved ANDA must comply with §314.80 regarding reporting and recordkeeping of adverse drug experiences, and must make reports required under §314.81 and section 505(k) of the Act for each approved abbreviated application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other responsibilities: withdrawal, change in ownership, waiver process
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must comply with §314.65 regarding withdrawal of an unapproved ANDA and §314.72 regarding change in ownership of an ANDA. An applicant may request FDA to waive any requirement under §§314.92–314.99 and must meet waiver procedures under §314.90.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If FDA grants a waiver for a requirement under §§314.92–314.99, the waived requirement will not be a basis for refusal to approve an ANDA under §314.127.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial review cycle timeframe (180 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided otherwise, within 180 days of receipt of an NDA under §505(b) or an ANDA under §505(j), FDA will review it and send either an approval letter or a complete response letter; this 180-day period is called the 'initial review cycle.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initial review cycle may be adjusted by mutual agreement or as provided elsewhere (e.g., due to a major amendment).

rubrics_metrics.name: NDA filing and ANDA receipt threshold determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days after FDA receives an NDA, the Agency will determine whether the NDA may be filed (a threshold determination that it's sufficiently complete to permit substantive review). An ANDA will be evaluated to determine whether it may be received (threshold determination that it's substantially complete).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If FDA finds none of the reasons for refusing to file/receive apply, it will file/receive and notify applicant. For 505(b)(2) or ANDAs with paragraph IV, applicant will be notified via paragraph IV acknowledgment letter. Applicants may be allowed to request informal conferences or to correct/resubmit following a refusal-to-file/receive decision; inaction may lead FDA to consider the submission withdrawn after 1 year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for refusing to file an NDA or consider an ANDA not received (deficiencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may refuse to file or not consider an ANDA received if: (1) application form incomplete; (2) not submitted in required form; (3) incomplete on its face (missing information required by statute/regulations); (4) missing complete environmental assessment or categorical exclusion info; (5) no accurate/complete English translation of non-English parts; (6) missing GLP compliance statements for nonclinical studies or explanations for noncompliance; (7) missing IRB/informed consent compliance statements for clinical studies or explanations; (8) drug already covered by approved NDA/ANDA where applicant has approved NDA/ANDA or is merely distributor/repacker; (9) NDA submitted as 505(b)(2) for a drug duplicate eligible under 505(j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA will consider the nature (major/minor) and number of deficiencies when determining whether an ANDA is incomplete on its face.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory prohibitions for filing/receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will refuse to file or consider an ANDA not received if: (1) the drug is subject to licensing under the Public Health Service Act and related subchapter, or (2) submission of a 505(b)(2) application or ANDA is not permitted under specified statutory provisions (e.g., certain 505A/505E circumstances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome of FDA review and hearing opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 180 days after filing (plus any extension), FDA will either approve the NDA or issue a notice of opportunity for a hearing if the applicant asked for a hearing in response to a complete response letter. For ANDAs, within 180 days after receipt (plus extension), FDA will approve or disapprove the ANDA and may issue a notice of opportunity for hearing if the applicant asked for one in response to a complete response letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These outcomes do not apply to NDAs/ANDAs that have been withdrawn by the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications during review: general principles and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: During review, FDA shall communicate with applicants about scientific, medical, and procedural issues via telephone, letters, or meetings, as appropriate; communications must be appropriately documented in the application per §10.65.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further procedures for communications are contained in a publicly available staff manual guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of easily correctable deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA reviewers shall make every reasonable effort to promptly communicate easily correctable deficiencies discovered in an application (particularly chemistry, manufacturing, and controls issues) to permit early correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This early communication is intended to allow submission of an amendment before the review period elapses. Major scientific issues are ordinarily not addressed by early communications but in a complete response letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ninety-day conference availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 90 days after receipt of the application, FDA will provide applicants an opportunity to meet with reviewing officials to inform them of the general progress and status of their applications and to advise applicants of deficiencies identified by that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This meeting is available for all new chemical entities and major new indications of marketed drugs; it is available at the applicant's option and may be by telephone if agreed. Ninety-day conferences are not ordinarily held on abbreviated applications (ANDAs).

rubrics_metrics.name: End-of-review conference
rubrics_metrics.description: At the conclusion of FDA's review of an NDA, as designated by issuance of a complete response letter, FDA will provide the applicant an opportunity to meet with reviewing officials to discuss what further steps are needed before approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for such meetings must be directed to the director of the division responsible for reviewing the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism for other meetings and discouragement of drop-ins
rubrics_metrics.description: Other meetings may be held with advance notice to discuss scientific, medical, and other issues; requests directed to the director of the responsible division. 'Drop-in' visits (unannounced) are discouraged except for urgent matters (e.g., important new safety issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA will attempt to grant requests that involve important issues and can be scheduled at mutually convenient times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispute resolution: administrative/procedural path
rubrics_metrics.description: When administrative or procedural disputes arise, the applicant should first try to resolve the matter with the reviewing division (beginning with the consumer safety officer). If unresolved, applicant may raise matter with the ombudsman to facilitate timely equitable resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate issues for ombudsman include scheduling, obtaining timely replies, and timely completion of pending reviews; further details in a staff manual guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispute resolution: scientific and medical disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Major scientific issues are ordinarily communicated in a complete response letter; the 'end-of-review' and 'ninety-day' conferences provide fora for resolving issues. For disputes at other times, applicants should discuss with responsible reviewing officials and may request meetings progressing from Division Director to Office Director to Center Director if unresolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may suggest FDA seek outside expert advice; FDA may invite advisory committee members or consultants; applicants may bring their own consultants. Major unresolved policy issues may be referred to standing advisory committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to DEA for drugs with abuse potential
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will inform the Drug Enforcement Administration under section 201(f) of the Controlled Substances Act when an application or abbreviated application is submitted for a drug that appears to have abuse potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval conditioned on absence of refusal reasons (cross-reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will approve an NDA and send an approval letter if none of the reasons in §314.125 for refusing to approve the NDA applies.
